summary: The assigned gfx950 cannot execute the affected CUDA topk.cu path. Current main already substitutes an exact cooperative HIP implementation on ROCm; its full-row overflow rescan was numerically verified beyond the 4096-candidate cliff. The CUDA source still contains the reported silent truncation mechanism, so no unvalidated CUDA patch was made.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact selected-score multiset versus torch.topk, index range and uniqueness, and fp16-high-byte threshold-bucket population at 64x65536, 64x262144, and 4x1048576. Wrong rows were 0 in every case; the latter two cases exceeded the 4096-entry capacity described by the issue.
Three independent ROCm exactness boundary/distribution cases from the checked-in test suite; 3 passed.
The loaded native extension contains the cooperative HIP top-k instantiation and fast_topk interface symbols.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed the numerical reproduction and focused tests; raw output is retained under reports/j-55470ca2b722/.

remaining_limitations: No CUDA GPU was assigned, so the affected CUDA topk.cu implementation was not executed and the reported CUDA failure was not independently reproduced.
The installed ROCm native extension was validated rather than rebuilt because no native source change was made.
The fixture validates the kernel API only; no DeepSeek V3.2 model weights, serving path, full-model semantics, or distributed workload were exercised.
The CUDA source still silently truncates threshold-bin candidates beyond SMEM_INPUT_SIZE; this report does not claim that CUDA is fixed.
